Grateful to have completed my 12-week internship with Amazon Web Services (AWS) Talent Acquisition! Coming into this internship with no recruiting experience, I learned every part of the recruiting process, from building Boolean searches and conducting recruiter phone screens to trying different outreach strategies and using AI tools to work more efficiently. Along the way, I sourced hundreds of candidates and gained a much greater appreciation for the impact recruiters have on building great teams. A huge thank you to Ellie Murphy and Alyssa Nolan for all of your guidance and support throughout the summer. I'm also so grateful for all of the amazing intern friends I made! Thank you to everyone on the AWS Talent Acquisition team for such an incredible summer, I had the best internship experience ever! #AWS #Amazon #Internship #TalentAcquisition #CareerGrowth

Today we're launching one of the most exciting ground up innovations in the agent landscape: Kiro Crew! What started as a side project inside Amazon (known as Meshclaw) grew into something tens of thousands of builders across the company relied on daily. It's now open source for everyone. Kiro Crew is a persistent, self-evolving workspace that keeps work moving, online or off. It's built for engineering work that goes beyond a single chat session, and spans repos, tools, and days. Kiro Crew remembers your project context and history across sessions, turns your corrections into durable lessons and reusable skills, and keeps recurring jobs running on schedules you set. Devs can run several efforts in parallel or hand work to subagents that report back, so nothing waits in line. Hundreds of contributors shared feedback with us, helping make this launch possible. See how you can build your crew: https://kiro.dev/crew/

🎬 STEMFlix Video Competition is now open! STEMise and STEMist are collaborating to run STEMFlix, a global short-form video competition for students who want to explain a STEM topic that attracts global attention. Think astrophysics, organic chemistry, AI, whatever you're into, and condense into a 30-90 second vertical video. Here's how it works: pick a topic, film a short video explaining it, post it to YouTube as a Short (can be unlisted) with the tag #stemflix , then submit your link through the registration form. A panel of judges will score entries on technical accuracy, clarity, creativity, and educational impact, and top submissions win prizes. It's open to students in middle and high school in any country. No background required. ✏️ Register: https://lnkd.in/g5txNbsA 💬 Questions or want updates: join our Discord at https://lnkd.in/g3fw4WSq or email stemflixofficial@gmail.com .

💰 $2,500 USD to help winners on their projects + $30,000 in prizes and credits. 🌍 STEMist Hacks IV is a free hackathon for students 13 to 18, anywhere in the world. This is our fourth year running it, and it's still free, still fully online, still open to all middle and high schoolers who want to build something. 🚀 Turn a weekend idea into something real. 🤝 Team up with other builders from 20+ countries. 🛠️ Build anything you want: apps, games, hardware, AI tools. 🏆 Compete across hardware and software tracks. 💻 All online, join from anywhere. 📅 July 31 to August 2, 2026. Grand prize sponsored by T-Mobile. If you've never done a hackathon, that's fine. Most of our participants haven't. We run Saturday morning workshops for beginners, and projects get judged on effort and creativity, not just how polished they are. 👇 Comment HACKS below and I'll send you the registration link. STEMist Education is a registered 501(c)(3).

My boss made a crazy gamble. No not on the World Cup. But on me, here’s how: 3 weeks ago, I joined vly.ai (YC F24) as Head of Growth. 2 weeks later, I was behind the camera filming vly.ai (YC F24) biggest company announcement in history: Now, we’re in the midst of building something new, an idea backed by YC and other angel investors. I can’t lie and say that I was certain this was going to entirely work out. But if there’s one lesson that always hits hard for me, it’s that uncertainty is always part of the process. I still have yet to make my boss’s gamble worth it. I haven’t even scratched the surface of growth work. But one thing I know is to ride that wave of uncertainty. If you’re curious about what we’re building next, let’s chat. More coming soon. (Me and Victor Cheng passing out Taiyaki and Krispy Kreme the day we launched our acquired announcement)
